headline: Self-storage plan for 85,000-square-foot Building 5 at One Oak Hill Road approved with conditions.
summary: The applicant, Bellman Capital Group, proposed 59 parking spaces, where zoning calls for 85. Conditions include no outside storage, a locked rear dumpster, and security cameras at the back of the building. Two moratoriums were recommended to City Council: one on commercial battery storage and one on large-scale data centers. Brew England's drive-through coffee shop was continued to December 17.
decisions: Approved the special permit and site plan for self-storage in Building 5 at One Oak Hill Road, with conditions, 7-0.
Continued the mixed-use complex proposal by Main Street Fitchburg Property Owner LLC.
Approved extending the Healing Center's hours at 346 River Street to 8 a.m. to 11 p.m.
Approved the permit modification and land transfer for four single-family homes at Zero Townsend Street.
Authorized Chantel to sign the A&R plan for Zero Townsend Street once the chair and Chantel are satisfied with the language.
Approved one more year, to November 21, 2027, for the marijuana product manufacturer at Six Cobbler Drive.
Continued the Brew England drive-through coffee shop at 432-504 John Fitch Highway to the December 17 meeting.
Continued the parking plan for six-unit housing at 20 and 24 Grand Street to December.
Recommended a 12-month moratorium on commercial battery energy storage systems.
Recommended a 12-month moratorium on large-scale data centers to the City Council.
Approved the 2027 meeting dates and filing deadlines, with May moved to the fourth Tuesday and December moved to the third Thursday.
discussion: Oak Hill self-storage: Members asked about rear trash, dumping near the river, and unpaid taxes. The applicant agreed to install rear security cameras, and the rear dumpster would be for staff use only.
Fire alarm in Building 4: Public speakers said the fire suppression system works but one alarm head needs replacing. The approval is subject to fire department satisfaction of any outstanding issues.

Battery storage moratorium: Public speakers said battery systems are safe and a pause is not needed. The pause would give the city time to write zoning rules, and the City Council makes the final decision.
Data center moratorium: A public speaker cited water use, diesel backup generators, and power demand in urging a pause. The recommendation goes to the City Council.

Brew England drive-through plans: The applicant's engineer estimated 80 trips in the morning peak hour and 30 in the afternoon. Members asked about dumpster placement and plaza access, and the applicant will return in December.
